correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the complete irreducible decomposition of \(\operatorname{AGL}(1,q)\): \(q-1\) linear characters and one irreducible representation of degree \(q-1\). Translation acts diagonally on nonzero additive Fourier modes and a primitive multiplier acts as a single \(q-1\)-cycle. The only two determinant terms yield the product of \(1+\psi(t)\) over nonzero frequencies plus the cycle sign. Character fibres give \(2^{p^{r-1}-1}\) for odd characteristic and zero for characteristic two; scalar factors multiply to \(2^{q-1}-(-1)^{q-1}\). For odd prime fields the nonlinear kernel is exactly one-dimensional by the cyclic recurrence and nonzero diagonal entries; it occurs \(q-1\) times in the regular representation. Standalone exact verifier completed 42 checks for field orders three, four, five, seven, eight, nine and eleven. Finite tests corroborate rather than prove the infinite-field claim.

value.rationale: This exact singularity criterion distinguishes odd prime fields from all proper extensions in an infinite canonical family of affine groups, with complete integer determinants and exact regular nullities. Infinitely many primes \(p\equiv2\pmod3\) yield singular three-tap convolution on groups of order \(p(p-1)\) with no elements of order three, so no order-three coset-cancellation explanation applies. The prime/extension transition is forced by nontrivial additive-character fibre multiplicities in a nonlinear Fourier block and is not an arbitrary substitution. The theorem applies only to specified primitive-multiplier supports, not a full all-support census.
